subject: ventures/mobile-home-park-valuation-calculator
professional: a manufactured-housing-community broker/underwriter (MHP acquisitions analyst) who builds a T-12 to pro forma and a lender-style DSCR check

evidence.correctness: Ran `node --test '*.test.mjs'` (22 pass). Recomputed independently in Python from the textbook definitions (NOI = EGI - expenses; value = NOI/cap; level-payment amortization PMT = P*r/(1-(1+r)^-n)), using the default inputs and a second input set the author's tests do not use. (1) NOI 162,740, value 1,914,588.24, implied cap 11.624% match calc.mjs exactly. (2) Loan 980,000, annual debt service 83,117.23, DSCR 1.958, cash on cash 18.96% match; PMT(100k,6%,30y)=599.5505 matches the standard value. (3) Break-even move-outs: NOI delta at +$40 rent for k=0..7 move-outs is +22,522 ... +883 (k=4) ... -4,526 (k=5), so break-even 4 matches; NOI after 2 move-outs 174,442.40 and value created 137,675.29 match. (4) Second set occupied=40, rent=600, cap 7%: NOI 174,332, value 2,490,457 match. No arithmetic error found. Capped at 3, not 4: arithmetic is right but the model is simplified (see domain).
evidence.completeness: README/page claims checked: NOI (works), value at cap rate (works), implied cap on asking (works), DSCR (works), cash on cash (works, labeled before closing costs), cap-rate by rent-increase grid (works, 5x5), rent-increase value net of move-outs and break-even move-outs (works), entirely client-side (page.test.mjs asserts no fetch/XHR; grep agrees), usage counting plus opt-out (usage.test.mjs passes). Stated-not-built items (T-12 CSV importer, printable summary, scenario comparison) are labeled 'not built' in VENTURE.yaml, so not counted against it. No stubs or TODOs found. Not exercised in a real browser (only the DOM wiring was read): index.html run() and fill() read as correct.
evidence.verification: 22 tests pass in ~190 ms. Seeded four mutations in calc.mjs, each reverted with git checkout (git status clean afterwards): (a) management fee on rentIncome instead of EGI: 2 tests failed (caught); (b) monthly rate divisor 12 -> 11: 1 failed (caught); (c) amortization exponent -n -> -n-1: 1 failed (caught); (d) implied cap *1.01 plus fixed+1 in the full-occupancy NOI: 1 failed, the fixed+1 part is uncaught because the full-occupancy test only asserts full.noi > base.noi. Hand-worked defaults in the test comments were verified correct. Gaps: no test of the grid values, the cap-rate filter, ltv/amort inputs at the page level, or the page's input fallback. Tests check page text with regexes rather than driving the DOM.
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs, calc.test.mjs, page.test.mjs, usage.mjs, index.html script. calc.mjs is small, pure and clean with sensible guards (nz(), capped occupancy, blank inputs do not throw). Defects: (1) index.html opts() silently replaces any blank or unparseable input with the placeholder default (num NaN -> DEFAULTS[k]), so a cleared lot-rent or asking-price box computes with 450 or 1,400,000 and shows no warning; for a tool whose users type numbers from a seller's T-12 this is a silent-wrong-number path. (2) occupied > lots is capped (warned), but negative or non-numeric values are coerced to 0 with no warning (nz). (3) The expense parser requires 'label, amount' lines and reports skipped lines (good). (4) Page logic lives inline in index.html and is untested except by regex. (5) llms.txt links the retired github.io address, not marisstella.app.
evidence.claims: Backed: free/client-side/no upload (page.test.mjs, grep for network calls), MIT (LICENSE present), disclaimer and 'Not decided' section present and tested, usage event names match code (tested), defaults stated as placeholders. Limits are listed honestly in README and page (no cap-rate data, no rent control, no reassessment, expenses fixed with occupancy). Unbacked or stale: (1) llms.txt points to duncan-haywood.github.io/oss-monorepo/..., the old Pages address that now only redirects, per CLAUDE.md hosting; (2) FAQ says 'Lenders typically want a cushion above 1.0' which is true but vague (no 1.20-1.25 convention for MHP loans); (3) README says 'Entirely client-side' yet loads usage counters in localStorage, which the page does disclose. (4) kill criterion and hypothesis are untested, stage 'prototype' is honest. No fabricated reviews or numbers.
evidence.fitness: Walked a buyer's job: type 60 lots / 51 occupied / $450 rent and a six-line T-12, get NOI, value, implied cap 11.6% vs asking, DSCR 1.96, and the +$40 increase result with 4 break-even move-outs: works in under a minute, and the break-even move-out count is the useful, differentiating output. Where a buyer stalls: no vacancy/credit-loss line on top of physical occupancy, no utility-reimbursement scaling, no property-tax reassessment on sale, no closing costs or capex/infrastructure line, loan sized from asking price rather than lesser of LTV and DSCR sizing, no price-vs-value-to-offer solve, no export or save, no T-12 import. Fine for a first-pass screen, not for a lender package or an offer.
evidence.domain: Compared against standard MHC underwriting (NOI = EGI less expenses, capitalized at a market cap rate; lenders add a 5-10% vacancy/credit loss floor, 5-10% management on EGI, $100-300 per lot reserves, reassessed property tax, and size loans to the lesser of LTV, DSCR ~1.20-1.25 and debt yield). The core capitalization and break-even logic is correct and the management-on-EGI, reserves-per-lot and 'seller leaves out management/reserves' advice is what a practitioner says. Departures a broker would flag in the first hour: (1) EGI uses actual occupied lots with no separate vacancy/bad-debt allowance and holds 'other income' (utility reimbursements, which scale with occupancy) fixed while water/sewer is also fixed, so the move-out penalty is understated on the income side and break-even is optimistic for utility-heavy parks; (2) rent-increase value assumes every remaining tenant pays the full increase immediately (no phase-in, no tenant-owned vs park-owned home split, no notice period); (3) loan sizing ignores DSCR constraint; (4) no price-per-pad comparison to a comp set, beyond price per lot. All of these are disclosed as 'not decided' or 'held fixed', which is why this is 2 and not 1.

defects.what: Blank or unparseable input fields are silently replaced with the placeholder default (cleared lot rent runs as $450, cleared asking price as $1,400,000) with no warning, so a user can read a result computed on numbers they did not type.

Model has no vacancy/credit-loss line and holds other income (utility reimbursements) fixed while occupancy falls, so rent-increase break-even move-outs are optimistic for parks with utility billing; disclosed only as 'expenses other than management are held fixed'.
Loan is sized as LTV x asking price only, with no DSCR or debt-yield test, so the financing block can show a loan a lender would not write.
llms.txt links the retired github.io address instead of https://marisstella.app/mobile-home-park-valuation-calculator/.
Tests do not pin the value grid, the full-occupancy NOI value (a +1 mutation there survived), or page-level input handling.

verdict: A small, honest, arithmetically correct first-pass MHP screen: every output I recomputed independently (NOI, value, implied cap, PMT, DSCR, cash on cash, break-even move-outs, a second input set) matched exactly, 22 tests pass, and 3 of 4 seeded mutations were caught. It does not meet the senior-professional bar overall (median of scores is 2) because claims and craft carry real gaps: a silent default-substitution on blank inputs, a stale llms.txt URL, and a model that omits vacancy/credit loss, scales neither utility income nor payroll with occupancy, and sizes the loan without a DSCR test, so a broker would use it to screen but not to price or present a deal. It is finished against what it claims (stage: prototype, unbuilt features labeled), not expert-grade.
